idea: Week three, from the story bank: written from the source, then corrected by two independent editors before voicing.
description: In the Fourth All India Handloom Census, 2019-20, Assam had 11,07,428 of India's 26,73,891 handloom weavers: 41%, the highest of any state, and three for every one in West Bengal, the next state (3,66,656).

A second Ministry of Textiles table puts 44% of India's handlooms in Assam; that table gives no reference year. State totals, not per person. The figures were given by the Ministry of Textiles in Lok Sabha answers of 5 and 19 August 2025.
source: Ministry of Textiles, Government of India, reply to Lok Sabha Unstarred Question No. 4300 of 19 August 2025 (Handloom Weavers), Annexure-1: State/UT-wise number of handloom weavers and allied workers, as per the Fourth All India Handloom Census 2019-20 (the all-India row printed in the table, 26,73,891 weavers, is the total used for the shares; 31 rows are printed and add up to it exactly; 30 are read, because Jammu and Kashmir, printed together with Ladakh as one row of 15,784, is not read). Looms: Lok Sabha Starred Question No. 237 of 5 August 2025 (Textiles), Annexure-I, 'State-wise number of handlooms, handloom workers and handicraft artisans', a second Ministry table; the answer gives no reference year for the loom count, but its 'handloom workers' column equals the Census 'total handloom workers' column row for row (35,22,512 in all). State totals, not per-person figures.
